Elena (CEO): Thanks everyone for coming — quick follow-up from the all-hands: we want to use this thread for any strategic clarifying questions about mission/positioning/roadmap. Ask away and Ravi and I will answer.
Maya (Sales): Quick one — when we say 'serving is the moat', what should I say to customers who ask how we're different from cloud vendors' managed endpoints?
Elena (CEO): Good question. Short answer: we focus on production economics and predictable behavior for LLMs — not just access. So emphasize latency SLOs, cost controls (batching, caching), and routing/fallbacks that large clouds don't productize end-to-end today.
Priya (Eng): Follow-up: any guidance on when to pitch Dedicated vs Hosted to startups?
Ravi (VP Product): For startups: start with Hosted for time-to-value. Push Dedicated when predictable throughput or data isolation becomes a gating factor — usually when monthly spend or latency SLAs hit a certain threshold. We should work with Sales to codify numeric triggers.
Jonah (SRE): Are we locking any latency SLO tiers for Dedicated customers? Ops asked for explicit numbers to communicate to prospects.
Elena (CEO): Yes — Dedicated has SLA-backed p50/p95 targets per plan. We'll publish the baseline SLA in the docs next week. For prospects, give ranges until the public page is up.
Sam (DevEx): Can we get a one-liner for messaging about 'why not open-source runtime' vs our platform? Customers ask about self-hosting.
Ravi (VP Product): One-liner: open-source runtimes solve part of the stack; we solve predictable global operations, cost engineering, and rollouts across hosted/dedicated/private with observability and built-in fallbacks.
Carlos (Eng): On the technical side: any change to the priority between Optimize (cost tooling) vs Runtime reliability in next quarter roadmap?
Ravi (VP Product): We shifted some focus to runtime reliability after the last incidents thread. Q2 priorities: 60% reliability/observability work, 25% Optimize features, 15% integrations. We’ll publish a short roadmap doc.
Lila (PM): Will the roadmap doc include compatibility notes for common open models and quantized variants? That helps Sales/SEs.
Ravi (VP Product): Yes — compatibility matrix and recommended quant profiles per workload will be in the doc.
Maya (Sales): Competitor question: how worried should we be about big cloud offering discounted GPU endpoints?
Elena (CEO): We watch pricing, but our edge is predictable unit economics and developer ergonomics that reduce total spend. Also we have specialized inference kernels and routing logic that they don’t expose. We expect competing offers, but our strategy is to be the easiest way to get predictable production inference.
Priya (Eng): Any changes to model support cadence? People ask when new open models get added to the catalog.
Ravi (VP Product): We’ll keep a biweekly cadence for onboarding high-traction open models, prioritized by internal telemetry + partner requests.
Jonah (SRE): For private deployments, how much of the control plane is customer-managed vs our managed piece?
Elena (CEO): Private = customer-managed networking + optional on-prem agents; control plane can be run by us or by the customer in a hybrid mode depending on compliance needs. We'll add an FAQ.
Maya (Sales): request: can we get a short cheatsheet for objections vs cloud + vs OSS?
Sam (DevEx): I can draft a one-page cheatsheet if Product approves the bullets.
Ravi (VP Product): Please do — Sam, let's sync Tuesday. I'll share the initial bullets.
hq-bot: Reminder: all-hands follow-up doc posted: https://redwood.internal/all-hands/2899990001 (internal link).
Elena (CEO): Thanks all — we’ll follow up with the roadmap doc and the SLA/cheatsheet next week. If you have tactical asks (scripts, decks), ping Sam. :thumbsup:
